output.brief: The latency regression is almost certainly caused by the 2 Nov storage compaction tuning change, not by gateway 5.8. The change raised compaction threads from 2 to 6. Disk utilisation went from 41% to 97% within minutes, and node-side GET time rose from 61 to 262 ms. Every cell that got the change jumped within 5–15 minutes, regardless of when it received 5.8. aps-3 skipped the change and stayed at about 94 ms even though it runs 5.8. Rolling euw-1 back to 5.7 changed nothing. The network showed no matching problem. Traffic growth was small. Do not roll back the gateway fleet. It would remove the security fix, with an audit deadline of 30 Nov, and would not help. Do not pause compaction. Backlog was 11% on 2 Nov and the limit is about 15%, so a long pause risks disk-full. Next step: revert the tuning in one cell, watch p99 and backlog, then extend the revert to the others. Consider a gentler compaction setting rather than 6 threads. Hold off on limiting Orrin's ingest until the 10 Nov backlog attribution comes in. I'm fairly confident in this diagnosis. The main open question is what drove the backlog growth.
